finding.claim: iconUrl is stored without any validation and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job, allowing an attacker to make the server issue GET requests to arbitrary URLs (internal hosts, cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/, localhost services). The response body is read as bytes, so it may also be exposed or processed.
finding.source: The `icon` parameter of Profile.update, populated from the PUT /profile request body

trace.note: update(webhook, icon): `icon` is attacker-controlled from PUT /profile
this.iconUrl = icon, stored with no validation of scheme, host or IP
sync() passes iconUrl to URI.create and issues a GET via HttpClient, with the body read as a byte array

finding.guards_checked: Only `webhook` is validated (regex at line 12 pins it to https://hooks.example.com/ plus 20 alphanumerics; String.matches is a full match, so the webhook sink at line 21 is not exploitable). `icon` has no scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking and no DNS-rebinding protection. No other validation exists in the codebase (single file).

verdict.reason: Profile.java:16 stores the PUT /profile `icon` with no validation (only `webhook` is checked at line 12), and Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl), so no closing guard exists on this path.
